### `Accessibility`

```csharp
AccessibilityMode Accessibility { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the accessibility / tagged-PDF conformance mode. Default `None` - the writer produces an untagged PDF and ignores all tagging machinery. Set to `PdfUa1` (PDF 1.7) or `PdfUa2` (PDF 2.0) to opt the document into tagged output (structure tree, MCIDs, XMP conformance claim, `/Lang`, `/MarkInfo`).

Orthogonal to `Conformance`: a document can be PDF/A, PDF/UA, both, or neither. PDF/UA-2 combines with `PdfA4` only; PDF/UA-1 with PDF/A-1, -2 and -3.

### `Conformance`

```csharp
PdfAConformance Conformance { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the PDF/A archival conformance level. Default `None` - the document is a normal PDF.

When set to any non-`None` value, the serializer auto-upgrades `Version` to PDF 1.7 (PDF/A emission requires PDF 1.7), embeds the sRGB ICC profile, emits the matching `/OutputIntents` entry, and writes a `pdfaid:part` / `pdfaid:conformance` XMP block.

"a" levels (`PdfA1a`, `PdfA2a`, `PdfA3a`) require `Accessibility` = `PdfUa1`; the serializer throws `PdfAConformanceException` otherwise.

Honest-claim behaviour: setting this to a non-None value is a request, not a guarantee. The serializer suppresses the `pdfaid` XMP block and `/OutputIntents` entry whenever the document references any of the standard 14 fonts (Helvetica, Times-*, Courier-*, Symbol, ZapfDingbats), because PDF/A §6.3.4 requires every font to be embedded and BonniePDF does not bundle subset versions of those faces. To actually produce a PDF/A-conformant file, register a real TTF via `TtfFont.FromFile()` / `FontMetrics.RegisterFontAlias()` (or rely on the bundled Liberation faces) and use that for every text element.

### `DefaultTextStyle`

```csharp
TextStyle DefaultTextStyle { get; set; }
```

Default text style applied to all text elements that have not had their style properties explicitly set. Use this to define a document-wide font/size/color baseline and avoid repeating style assignments on every element.

```csharp
settings.DefaultTextStyle = new TextStyle().WithFamily("Helvetica").WithSize(11).WithColor(ColorPalette.Slate[600]);
```

### `Language`

```csharp

```

Document natural language as a BCP-47 tag (e.g. `"en-GB"`, `"de-DE"`, `"fr"`). Written to the catalog as `/Lang` when set; required for PDF/UA-1 conformance, where it tells assistive tech the language of unmarked content. Default `null` (no language declared).

### `MaxImageDpi`

```csharp
int? MaxImageDpi { get; set; }
```

The most pixels per inch an embedded PNG image is kept at (default: 288). An image that carries more pixels than its printed size can use is reduced to this resolution when the document is written, by an exact area average that never re-encodes the image lossily and never enlarges it. `null` embeds every image at its source resolution. JPEG, indexed and 16-bit images are always embedded as they are; `Diagnostic` entries in `Diagnostics` report what was reduced and what was passed through.

### `MissingGlyphs`

```csharp
MissingGlyphs MissingGlyphs { get; set; }
```

What happens to a character no registered font can draw: `Drop` (the default) leaves it out and records a `Font` warning; `Throw` stops generation with a `MissingGlyphException`. A character that falls back to another font is not missing.

### `OversizedContent`

```csharp
OversizedContent OversizedContent { get; set; }
```

What happens to content that cannot split across pages and is taller than a page: `Clip` (the default) draws it at the top of a page, cut off at the bottom of the body, and records an error diagnostic; `Throw` stops generation with an `OversizedContentException`. Text, tables, lists and stacks split instead, so they are never oversized.

### `PageBackground`

```csharp
Func<int, IElement> PageBackground { get; set; }
```

Template function for the full-page background slot. Called with the page number (1-based); the returned element is painted behind all page content. Unlike `HeaderTemplate` / `FooterTemplate`, the background slot spans the entire page and ignores the margins, so bleed images, scanned letterhead, and certificate backgrounds reach the page edge. Rendered at the page origin (0, 0) with the full page width available.

### `PageColor`

```csharp
Color? PageColor { get; set; }
```

Background colour painted behind every page. When set, the render pipeline fills the entire page (origin 0,0, full width and height, ignoring margins) with this colour before anything else is drawn, so it sits behind the `PageBackground` slot, headers, body content, and footers. Leave `null` for a transparent (viewer-default, usually white) background.

This is the simple "page colour" shortcut; for textured or image backgrounds use `PageBackground` instead (or both — `PageColor` fills, `PageBackground` layers on top).

### `PageForeground`

```csharp
Func<int, IElement> PageForeground { get; set; }
```

Template function for the full-page foreground slot. Called with the page number (1-based); the returned element is painted on top of all page content (including headers and footers), making it ideal for "DRAFT"/"CONFIDENTIAL" overlays and stamps. Like `PageBackground` it spans the entire page and ignores the margins, rendered at the page origin (0, 0) with the full page width available.

### `PageLabel`

```csharp
PageLabel PageLabel { get; set; }
```

Page labelling configuration written as `/PageLabels` in the document catalog (PDF §12.4.2). Controls the number shown in the viewer's page counter and "go to page" dialog — not the printed text on the page itself.

Use when the document represents a subset of a larger work and the viewer counter should reflect the logical page numbering rather than the physical 1-based sheet count.

```csharp
Settings = new DocumentSettings { PageLabel = new PageLabel { StartAt = 42 } } // → viewer shows "42" on page 1, "43" on page 2, etc.
```

Note: the footer template still receives the physical page number. Offset it manually if you want the printed number to match: `FooterTemplate = n => new TextBlock { Text = (n + 41).ToString() }`

### `SvgRasterizer`

```csharp
Func<string, Task<byte[]>> SvgRasterizer { get; set; }
```

Renders SVG markup to PNG bytes, or null for none.

With one set, an `Svg` element whose `StrictUnsupportedFeatures` is false draws what the SVG importer cannot draw as vector content - filters, masks, stylesheets, ... - as images in their place, instead of skipping them. BonniePDF rasterizes nothing itself: any renderer will do. It is called on the async generate paths only; a synchronous generate whose document would need it fails rather than drawing something different.
